response.sql:
WITH status_avgs AS (
  SELECT t.equipstatus, AVG(s.pulsepersec) AS avg_pulse
  FROM signals s
  JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
  WHERE s.pulsepersec IS NOT NULL AND t.equipstatus IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY t.equipstatus
),
m1 AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_pulse) AS mean1 FROM status_avgs
),
kept1 AS (
  SELECT a.equipstatus, a.avg_pulse, a.avg_pulse - m1.mean1 AS excess1
  FROM status_avgs a
  CROSS JOIN m1
  WHERE a.avg_pulse > m1.mean1
),
m2 AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_pulse) AS mean2 FROM kept1
),
kept2 AS (
  SELECT k.equipstatus, k.avg_pulse, k.excess1, k.avg_pulse - m2.mean2 AS excess2
  FROM kept1 k
  CROSS JOIN m2
  WHERE k.avg_pulse > m2.mean2
)
SELECT AVG(avg_pulse) AS avg_pulse_average,
       AVG(excess1) AS avg_excess_over_mean1,
       AVG(excess2) AS avg_excess_over_mean2
FROM kept2;

assumptions.assumption: Signals with no matching telescope are dropped by the inner join. Each signal matches at most one telescope because telescregistry is the primary key, so no signal is counted twice.
Each status average is an unweighted mean over the statuses, and 'above' means strictly greater than the comparison mean.
Signals whose telescope has a NULL equipstatus are excluded, because a missing value is not a status. The request does not say how to treat them.
Statuses whose pulse rates are all NULL produce no average and are excluded, since the request says to ignore missing pulse rates.

The 'average excess' values are the mean of each remaining status's excess over the relevant mean. The first mean is the mean of all status averages, and the second is the mean of the averages kept in step one.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat signals whose telescope has a NULL equipstatus as their own status group rather than dropping them.
